page: Microsoft Azure D64d_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, utilizing hyper-threading with 2.0 threads per core. The server is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced memory-to-core ratio of 4.0 GB per core. It includes a bundled local SSD storage capacity of 2458 GB, but does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. While single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core CPU performance at 1899.49 and Geekbench single-core score at 1649.0, rank in the average tier, the multi-core capabilities are strong. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance reaches 62149.0, and the Geekbench multi-core score is 16422.0. Memory bandwidth is also strong for large block operations, with read-only large block bandwidth at 291.88 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 134.9 GB/sec. Additionally, the system demonstrates strong performance in database operations with a score of 30145.69 on Passmark and Redis SET operations achieving 62.01 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D64d_v5 offers high resource density with its 64 dedicated vCPUs and substantial 2.4 TB local SSD, making it a viable option for workloads requiring high local I/O performance without the premium of memory-optimized tiers. However, a key tradeoff is its average single-threaded performance and average LLM inference speeds, such as 22.11 tokens per second for text generation on a medium 7B model. This server is suited for multi-threaded workloads, software compilation, static web serving, database operations, and general-purpose enterprise applications that benefit from local SSD scratch space.
